title: Introduction to Paid Ads for Restaurants

facts.fact: The blog post 'Introduction to Paid Ads for Restaurants' was published on 24 September 2024.
The blog post 'Introduction to Paid Ads for Restaurants' is listed as a 3-minute read.
To start a Google search ads campaign, a restaurant needs a Google Ads Manager account with an attached debit or credit card.
facts.quote: you’ll need a Google Ads Manager account and an attached debit or credit card to begin placing search ads on your target keywords

facts.fact: Setting up a Google My Business profile for a restaurant costs nothing.
facts.quote: This costs nothing and is good idea regardless of whether you want to run a paid advertising campaign.

facts.fact: Selecting 'Performance Max' as the campaign type in Google Ads serves a restaurant's ads to users browsing Google Maps for their next meal.
facts.quote: By selecting “Performance Max” as a campaign type via Google Ads, any ads you run will be served to the most relevant users browsing Google Maps for their next meal.

facts.fact: The page recommends always having two or three ads running at any time within a Meta paid social campaign so the platform can optimise toward the best performers.
facts.quote: It’s important to always have two or three ads running at any time within your campaign, so that the platform can optimise

facts.fact: Meta Ads Manager reports campaign statistics such as the amount paid per user click and the amount spent per reservation.
facts.quote: providing statistics like the amount you pay per user click, or the amount you spend per reservation

facts.fact: Restaurants can set up Meta paid campaigns with goals such as traffic or reservations across Facebook, Instagram, or both.
facts.quote: restaurants can set up paid campaigns with specific goals like traffic or reservations across Facebook, Instagram or both.

facts.fact: Paid search ads for restaurants appear above regular search results.
facts.quote: These paid advertisements appear above regular search results, allowing advertising restaurants to gain an advantage over other competitors.

facts.fact: The most popular search keywords are also the most expensive keywords for restaurant search advertising.
facts.quote: However, the most popular search keywords are also the most expensive.

facts.fact: TheFork's blog reports that Michelin-star restaurant Benares Mayfair increased bookings by 20% with TheFork Festival.
facts.quote: How Michelin-star restaurant Benares Mayfair increased bookings by 20% with TheFork Festival!

facts.fact: TheFork Manager's page displays a 4.4 rating on Trustpilot, a third-party review platform.
TheFork Manager's page displays a 4.5 rating on the App Store, a third-party app marketplace.
TheFork Manager's page displays a 4.8 rating on the Play Store, a third-party app marketplace.
